# action.docker_container_run

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Runs a one-shot container to completion, like `docker run --rm`: creates it (pulling the image when missing), starts it, waits until it exits within `timeout`, reads its exit code and output, then removes it (`remove`, default `true`). The result object holds `exit_code`, `stdout` and `stderr` (the last `tail` lines; both sensitive). An exit code outside `expected_exit_codes` fails the action. Nothing attaches to the container; the output is read after the exit with `ContainerLogs`. To keep the exited container in state instead, use `docker_container` with `state = "exited"`.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_run.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_container_run" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_container_run.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_run.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binds` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Volume bindings (`HostConfig.Binds`), `<host path or volume>:<container path>[:ro]`, like `docker run -v`. |
| `command` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Command (`Config.Cmd`), exec form, e.g. `["sh", "-c", "echo hi"]`. Unset uses the image's `CMD`. |
| `entrypoint` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Entrypoint override (`Config.Entrypoint`). Unset uses the image's. |
| `env` | `map(string)` | optional |  |  | Environment variables (`Config.Env`), merged over the image's. |
| `expected_exit_codes` | `list(number)` | optional |  |  | Exit codes that count as success. Default `[0]`. |
| `image` | `string` | required |  |  | Image to run, e.g. `busybox:1.36` (`Config.Image`). Pulled with the provider's registry auth when not present locally. |
| `labels` | `map(string)` | optional |  |  | Container labels (`Config.Labels`). With the provider's `owner` set, the owner label is added. |
| `name` | `string` | optional |  |  | Container name. Unset lets the daemon generate one, so repeated runs never collide. |
| `network_mode` | `string` | optional |  |  | Network mode (`HostConfig.NetworkMode`): `bridge` (daemon default), `host`, `none`, `container:<name\|id>` or a network name. |
| `remove` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Remove the container after the run, also when it fails (`docker run --rm`). Default `true`. |
| `result_path` | `string` | optional |  |  | Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails. |
| `tail` | `number` | optional |  |  | Lines kept from the end of the output in `stdout` / `stderr` (the Engine's `tail`). Default `1000`. |
| `timeout` | `string` | optional |  |  | How long the run may take, as a Go duration (`30s`, `10m`). Default `5m`. On timeout the action fails and the container is removed (killed) when `remove` is true. |
| `user` | `string` | optional |  |  | User (and optional group) to run as (`Config.User`). |
| `working_dir` | `string` | optional |  |  | Working directory (`Config.WorkingDir`). |

## Example

```terraform
# Run a one-shot container like `docker run --rm`: create, start, wait for the
# exit, capture exit_code / stdout / stderr, remove. The apply fails unless the
# exit code is in expected_exit_codes.
action "docker_container_run" "migrate" {
  config {
    image   = "ghcr.io/org/migrate:2.1.0"
    command = ["migrate", "up"]
    env = {
      DATABASE_URL = "postgres://db:5432/app"
    }
    network_mode        = "app"
    timeout             = "15m"
    expected_exit_codes = [0]
    result_path         = "${path.module}/out/migrate.json"
  }
}

# Run it after the database container is created or replaced.
resource "docker_container" "db" {
  name  = "db"
  image = "postgres:17"

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_container_run.migrate]
    }
  }
}

# On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_run.migrate
```
